draft.title: Critical lenses
card: A critical lens is a way of reading a text that asks a particular kind of question. The same text can be read through different lenses, and each one brings different things into view.
Feminist and postcolonial
A feminist reading asks how a text shows gender and who holds power. A postcolonial reading asks how it shows colonial rule, culture and identity.
Marxist
asks how a text shows class, wealth and work, and who gains from the way society is arranged.
Psychoanalytic
asks what a text shows about the mind, such as hidden desires, fears and memories that shape a character.
draft.remember: A lens is a set of questions you bring to a text. Pick the one that gives you the most to argue.

a.q: A student reads a novel by asking how its wealthy and working-class characters are treated, and who benefits from the society shown. Which lens is this?
opts: Marxist
Feminist
Postcolonial
Psychoanalytic
a.why: Questions about wealth, work and who benefits from society belong to a Marxist lens. A feminist lens would focus on gender instead, which is not the focus of these questions.
a.clue: Think about which lens deals with class and wealth.

b.q: Mia is writing about a play in which a young man is haunted by a buried childhood fear that drives his choices. Which lens would help her most?
opts: Psychoanalytic, because it focuses on the mind
Marxist, because it focuses on wealth and work
Postcolonial, because it focuses on colonial rule
Feminist, because it focuses on gender and power
b.why: A buried fear shaping a character's choices is a question about the mind, which is what a psychoanalytic lens explores. A Marxist lens could still be applied to the play, but it would ask about class, not about this fear.
b.clue: Which lens asks about fears and memories inside a character?

b.best: Psychoanalytic, because it focuses on the mind

Feminist
Postcolonial
Psychoanalytic

a.clue: What divides the owners from the workers in this story?
